text: ELECTION BETTING BOOM: WILL PREDICTION MARKETS SHAPE AMERICA’S 2026 MIDTERMS? Prediction markets are surging ahead of the 2026 U.S. elections, with platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket attracting growing volumes of political trading. Supporters argue that these markets aggregate information and provide a real-time gauge of voter sentiment, but critics warn that heavy financial activity could distort perceptions of candidates and races. The big test in 2026 will be whether trading merely predicts election outcomes or actually influences them. Officials and regulators are concerned that wealthy traders could manipulate odds, spread misleading signals or undermine confidence in the electoral process. With states and federal regulators still battling over how prediction markets should be governed, the midterms could become a major real-world experiment in whether election betting changes political behavior—and potentially results.

text: TRUMP’S 20% GDP DREAM: A GROWTH RATE AMERICA HAS SEEN ONLY ONCE SINCE WWII President Donald Trump has said U.S. economic growth could reach 20%, but that would be an extraordinary outlier by historical standards. Data going back to 1947 show that only one quarter has ever recorded annualized real GDP growth of 20% or more—the third quarter of 2020, when the economy rebounded at a 34.9% annualized rate after the pandemic shutdowns caused a historic contraction. The contrast with current conditions is stark: U.S. real GDP grew at just 1.5% annualized in Q2 2026. While the administration points to tax cuts, investment and productivity gains as potential growth drivers, economists generally view sustained growth anywhere near 20% as extremely unlikely. The 2020 surge was largely a rebound from an unprecedented collapse, making it a poor benchmark for normal economic expansion
